title: Uptime Budget Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Uptime Budget Record within the Platform Reliability and Availability Database. Models uptime, failure rates, repair times and maintenance needs. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record is arithmetic on observed history: failures over operating time give a failure rate, repair durations give a repair time, and the two combine into availability. Models are only as good as their inputs, so each record states its observation window and its sample size alongside the result.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: mean time between failures hours: 405. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A sustainment planner uses these records to set maintenance intervals, to size spares, and to judge whether a platform can meet its availability target with the maintenance it actually receives. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Uptime Budget Record: compute availability from failure and repair history.
mtbf_hours = 405
mttr_hours = 3
availability = mtbf_hours / (mtbf_hours + mttr_hours)
print("mean time between failures hours:", mtbf_hours)
print("mean time to repair hours:", mttr_hours)
print("availability:", round(availability, 5))
print("expected downtime hours per year:", round((1 - availability) * 8760, 1))
demo_output:
mean time between failures hours: 405
mean time to repair hours: 3
availability: 0.99265
expected downtime hours per year: 64.4

fields.model_used: failure rate and repair time arithmetic
